beats.say: Dollar Tree sells everything for a dollar. And some things cost $1.25.
A shelf of $1 items that fill the cart.
A handful of $3 novelties that look like a treat.
A few $5 basics that promise more.
In 2021 it raised the standard price to $1.25, a 25% increase. Looks like a mistake.
But it does a job: the single-price anchor.
The $1 baseline makes every higher tag feel premium, so you stay in the store.
When $1 became $1.25, $3 feels like a small step up, not a splurge.
You stop comparing each item; you just grab the $1-ish stuff.
You see it everywhere. A coffee shop offers $2 plain, $2.20 specialty, $5 combo.
A gym lists $10 day, $12 class pack, $30 month.
The middle option now feels like a smart upgrade.
When one price dominates, question what the other choices really sell. Follow for more.
